The complete published tables are reproduced by the embedded Python verifier. Finite exhaustive proof needs no extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Published research searches, open primary full texts and arithmetic comparisons reveal the distinction: preexisting geometric tritangent types, min-distance extrema and line multiplicities do not imply the exact 10-/11-value hyperplane-section frequency histograms. residual_risks: The complete 1981 Hirschfeld chapter could not be inspected and might contain an earlier equivalent small-field section table, although its accessible summary states only point/line statistics.

Boguslavskii original was read in relevant parts, not cover-to-cover; general extrema do not by themselves imply the present distribution.

value.rationale: The q=7 and q=11 models are naturally singled out as the only smooth characteristic >5 finite-field Clebsch models with no rational point off the geometric lines. The full hyperplane-section distribution is a complete, non-obvious invariant of those two exceptional arithmetic geometries and gives entire distinct evaluation-code spectra, beyond known total point/line multiplicities or maximal section sizes; the 13/30 rational S5 orbit certification makes the exact numbers reusable. The restriction is a motivated two-case classification rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
